name: CR-Diff-06-chain-3.d
generalfeedback:
In order to solve this problem we will have to use the chain rule <hint>calc_chain_rule</hint> as follows:

Define \(f({{CT:2}})={{CT:3}}\) and \(g({{CT:2}})={{CT:4}}\).

So \(f({{CT:2}})=ln(g({{CT:2}}))\). So,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
  \frac{d}{d{{CT:2}}}[{{CT:3}}] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{df}{dg}\cdot \frac{dg}{d{{CT:2}}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{d}{dg}[ln(g)]\cdot \frac{d}{d{{CT:2}}}({{CT:4}}) \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:5}}\cdot {{CT:6}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \left[{{CT:7}}\right][{{CT:6}}] \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:8}}
 \end{array}\]

on_true.feedback: You need to use the chain rule so that \[\frac{d}{dx}[f(g(x))]=\frac{df}{dg}\cdot \frac{dg}{dx}\] but you have not included the \(\frac{dg}{dx}\) term.
